properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research (relayed by Anthony 2026-08-06), specifically Graphify (Tree-sitter static analysis plus LLM semantic extraction) and Understand Anything (multi-agent pipeline over every file, function, class and dependency, with architectural-layer and business-domain views on top). STILL OPEN.

THE IDEA: the adopt skill currently recovers an existing system by having an agent read it. The survey's tools do the structural half MECHANICALLY and deterministically — files, functions, classes, imports, calls, API surfaces, DB models — and spend the LLM only on summaries. Splitting adopt the same way would make the cheap half cheap and exact, and leave the agent doing only what the artifact cannot tell you: why it was built that way, who asked for it, what is now vestigial. It would also make link-artifacts and reconcile_artifacts far cheaper to keep true, since registering artifacts and their hashes is precisely a mechanical sweep.

WHAT IS CHEAP: the extraction itself is a solved problem with off-the-shelf parsers, and it is deterministic, which sits well with req:deterministic-core.

WHAT IS EXPENSIVE: a parser per language, kept current — and Anthony's real operating context is a ten-year-old Python stack (bluesky, tiled) plus beamline analysis code, so the language surface is not small and much of it is dynamic, where static analysis is weakest.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is the strong one, from reflow2's own record: dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition already decided that reflow2's systems are FUNCTIONAL, not its file tree. Mechanical extraction from source produces exactly the decomposition that decision rejected — a Component per module, an Interface per public signature — which is a map of the repository, not of the design. Feeding that in would populate the graph with structure at the wrong altitude, and the wrong altitude is harder to fix than an empty graph because it looks finished. Understand Anything's "architectural layers (API, service, data, UI)" is an attempt at the same altitude problem, and it solves it by guessing, which is what dec:views-are-projections forbids reflow2 from doing.

A NARROWER VERSION THAT MAY SURVIVE THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: extract only ARTIFACTS and their content hashes, not Components or Interfaces. That is the layer whose identity genuinely IS the file, so no altitude claim is being made, and it is the layer reflow2 already models as files (art:*, set_artifact_checksum, cap:link-artifacts). The mechanical pass would then answer "what exists on disk and has it changed" and say nothing about what the design means. Offered as a distinction to consider, not as advocacy.

RELATED, NOT THE SAME QUESTION: whether reflow2 should CONSUME an existing code-graph tool's output rather than build extraction itself. The survey's tools all expose their graph over MCP, which would make them an ingest source rather than a rival. Unexplored.
properties.name: OPEN — should adopt extract code STRUCTURE mechanically (tree-sitter style) and reserve the agent for intent, when reflow2 has already decided decomposition is functional and not the file tree?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea because the mechanical/intent split is a genuinely good shape that the adopt skill does not currently have, and recording it with dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition named beside it is the point — the objection is what makes this idea usable later, and an idea killed in conversation would have lost it.
